items.followUp: What is the effect of pH and temperature on enzyme activity?

rubric.why: Shows how an enzyme lowers the activation energy.
rubric.description: Explains that enzyme-substrate binding provides a route that requires less activation energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the enzyme-substrate complex or an alternative lower-energy pathway.

rubric.why: The question also asks for two factors affecting enzyme activity.
rubric.description: Names any two factors that affect enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two valid factors.

modelAnswer: An enzyme binds its substrate to form an enzyme-substrate complex, providing a pathway with lower activation energy.
Two factors affecting enzyme activity are temperature and pH.

items.followUp: Describe how an enzyme-substrate complex forms and name two factors that affect enzyme activity.

rubric.why: The induced-fit model involves the substrate binding at an enzyme's active site, which is flexible.
rubric.description: States that the substrate binds to the enzyme's active site, which is not a rigid, exact fit beforehand.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substrate binding to a flexible active site.

rubric.why: Binding induces a change in the enzyme's shape so it fits the substrate more closely.
rubric.description: Explains that substrate binding changes the enzyme's shape to fit the substrate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the induced shape change and improved fit.

modelAnswer: In the induced-fit model, the enzyme's active site is flexible rather than a perfectly fixed fit for the substrate.
When the substrate binds, it induces a change in the enzyme's shape so the active site fits it closely.

items.followUp: Define digestion and distinguish it from the nutrients produced by digestion.

rubric.why: Nutrition describes the process by which an organism obtains and uses food.
rubric.description: Defines nutrition as a process of obtaining and using food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of nutrition.

rubric.why: Nutrients are the useful substances present in food that the body needs.
rubric.description: Defines nutrients as substances or food components needed by the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of nutrients.

modelAnswer: Nutrition is the process by which an organism obtains food and uses it for energy, growth and repair.
Nutrients are the useful chemical substances in food that the body needs.

items.followUp: Name two functions of calcium in the human body.

rubric.why: Calcium is an important mineral component of bones and teeth.
rubric.description: Identifies calcium's role in forming or maintaining bones and teeth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for bones and teeth.

rubric.why: Calcium also has important roles in clotting, muscle activity and nerve function.
rubric.description: Names another valid role of calcium in the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for blood clotting, muscle contraction or nerve function.

modelAnswer: Calcium is needed for the formation and maintenance of bones and teeth.
It is also needed for blood clotting and normal muscle contraction.

items.followUp: Define transpiration and name two environmental factors that affect its rate.

rubric.why: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, especially through stomata.
rubric.description: Defines transpiration as loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for water vapour loss from leaves or other aerial parts.

rubric.why: Several environmental conditions affect the rate of transpiration.
rubric.description: Names any two factors affecting transpiration rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid factors, such as temperature, humidity, wind or light.

modelAnswer: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata of leaves.
Its rate is affected by temperature, humidity, wind and light intensity.

items.followUp: Explain how sugars are transported from a source to a sink in plants.

rubric.why: Sugar loading at a source causes water to enter the phloem and raises its pressure.
rubric.description: States that sugar loading at the source creates high pressure in the phloem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the high-pressure condition at the source.

rubric.why: The pressure difference drives phloem sap from source to sink.
rubric.description: States that sap moves through the phloem down the pressure gradient towards a sink.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for pressure-driven movement from source to sink.

modelAnswer: In the pressure-flow mechanism, sugars are loaded into the phloem at a source, causing water to enter and creating high pressure.
This pressure difference drives phloem sap from the source towards a sink, where sugars are unloaded.

items.followUp: How can a low platelet count affect a person with dengue fever?

rubric.why: Dengue fever can reduce the number of platelets in the blood.
rubric.description: States that dengue causes a decrease in platelet count.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the reduced platelet count.

rubric.why: A low platelet count reduces the blood's ability to clot and can lead to bleeding.
rubric.description: States the consequence of low platelets, such as impaired clotting or bleeding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid consequence.

modelAnswer: Dengue fever can cause the platelet count in the blood to fall.
With fewer platelets, blood clotting is impaired and the risk of bleeding increases.

items.followUp: Explain five careers in biology other than medicine.

rubric.why: Biological knowledge is used to improve crops and agricultural production.
rubric.description: Explains agriculture as applying biology to crops or farming.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid explanation of a biology career in agriculture.

rubric.why: Forestry applies biological knowledge to the care and management of forests.
rubric.description: Explains forestry as the study, care or management of forests.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid explanation of forestry.

rubric.why: Biology is used to manage fisheries and breed or raise fish.
rubric.description: Explains fisheries or aquaculture as work involving fish and their production or management.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid explanation of fisheries or fish farming.

rubric.why: Biology supports the breeding, care and improvement of domestic animals.
rubric.description: Explains animal husbandry or a related animal-care career.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid explanation involving livestock or animal care.

rubric.why: Biotechnology uses organisms or biological processes to make useful products.
rubric.description: Explains biotechnology as the use of organisms or biological processes for useful purposes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid explanation of biotechnology.

modelAnswer: Agriculture: Biologists help improve crop varieties and increase crop production.
Forestry: Foresters use biological knowledge to conserve and manage forests.
Fisheries: Fisheries workers manage fish populations and develop fish farming.
Animal husbandry: Specialists breed, raise and improve livestock for useful products.
Biotechnology: Biotechnologists use organisms or biological processes to produce useful products.
